question: An aeroplane flies along the sides of an equilateral triangle at the speed of 300 km/h, 200 km/h and 240 km/h, respectively. The average speed of the plane while flying around the triangle is:
solution:
**Given:**

An aeroplane flies along the sides of an equilateral triangle at the speed of 300 km/h, 200 km/h, and 240 km/h, respectively.

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total distance / Total time

**Calculation:**

Let each side of the equilateral triangle be d km.

Total distance = 3d

Time taken to fly along each side:

Time₁ = d / 300

Time₂ = d / 200

Time₃ = d / 240

Total time = (d / 300) + (d / 200) + (d / 240)

⇒ Total time = d (1/300 + 1/200 + 1/240)

⇒ Total time = d (0.0125)

Average speed = Total distance / Total time

⇒ Average speed = 3d / (d × 0.0125)

⇒ Average speed = 3 / 0.0125

⇒ Average speed = 240 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**
